name: Flexential Minneapolis-Chaska (ViaWest)

model_completeness.definition: All eight contribution-account categories contain sourced or labeled modeled values, and GDP, employment, and wage county-comparison modules are populated. Comparison gaps are descriptive and do not establish causal facility effects.

research_value: ViaWest's April 2014 adaptive-reuse opening provides a development anchor; later Flexential expansions remain separately scoped.

history.date_note: This is a stored historical observation. Completion, grand opening, lease and operating-by dates are not automatically commissioning dates. Campus timing does not date every building.

research_updates.title: Investment audit and project boundary correction
research_updates.notes: Source families checked: City development bulletins, Agenda Center and Archive Center; ViaWest, Flexential and Stream history; county ownership; Minnesota eCRV; contemporary coverage; and current operator materials for 2013-2026. Queries used ViaWest, Flexential, Stream, 3500 Lyman, 1706 and 1708 West Creek, Entegris and parcel 30.0590020. City evidence places ViaWest's adaptive reuse at the former Entegris headquarters, 3500 Lyman Boulevard, while Stream identifies separate facilities at 1706 and 1708 West Creek Lane. The exact parcel eCRV search returned no record, but public coverage begins after the reported 2013 acquisition; agenda/archive searches are metadata-bounded. The opening release supports only a greater-than-$60 million source projection, not realized investment. No acquisition price, final conversion cost, audited capital ledger or annual facility capital series was located. Append-only fragments cannot correct the base aggregate: reassign clm_study_chaska_stream_rebate_2020, clm_study_chaska_stream_rebate_2021, clm_study_chaska_stream_rebate_2022, clm_study_chaska_stream_rebate_2023, clm_study_chaska_stream_rebate_2024 and clm_study_chaska_stream_rebate_2025 to the separate Stream Minneapolis I / West Creek project, or remove them from this target before the next aggregate release. The target label should be normalized to 'Flexential Minneapolis-Chaska (ViaWest)' and opening timing to April 2014; candidate metadata is outside fragment scope.

source.title: Chaska City Hall Bulletin: ViaWest conversion of former Entegris headquarters
source.notes: City bulletin says ViaWest purchased the former Entegris headquarters at the northwest corner of Lyman Boulevard and Highway 41 and began converting the 120,000-square-foot building. The same bulletin separately describes Stream's planned data center, supporting a boundary distinction rather than an ownership link. The bulletin does not report realized investment, jobs, payroll, utility use or incentives.

research_updates.title: Construction audit adds three bounded permit estimates
research_updates.notes: Source families checked: City SmartGov parcel, permit and inspection records; City archives and agendas; contractor cases; operator expansion materials; and contemporary construction coverage. Exact-address and parcel searches found B24-1109 ($5,861,872, PCL, issued January 23, 2025, unclosed), M24-0677 ($1,272,191, Metropolitan Mechanical/API HVAC, issued the same day, expired unclosed) and M26-0403 ($293,000, Climate Makers/EVER, issued August 10, 2026, open with final partially approved). These are administrative estimated values including labor, not paid costs, payroll, worker counts, completion or original conversion investment. Possible overlap between B24-1109 and M24-0677 is unresolved, so no portfolio sum is created. Related P26-0523 ($3,000) is excluded as overlapping M26-0403; BP26-0072 has no value; cancelled/expired B24-0504 ($150,000) is excluded. SmartGov's displayed history begins in 2022, so original conversion records require a City request.

source.title: City of Chaska permit B24-1109, Flexential Phase 5 Refresh
source.notes: Official SmartGov record identifies a commercial alteration at 3500 Lyman Boulevard described as 'Phase 5 Refresh - Alteration to Existing Building.' It reports estimated value including labor of $5,861,872, issued status on January 23, 2025, an unclosed permit with January 31, 2027 expiration, and PCL Construction Services Inc. as primary contractor. Portal inspections show approved hydrostatic testing on October 1, 2025 and approved footings on June 5, 2025, with a foundation-reinforcement item pending, a slab item cancelled and multiple finals blank. The amount is an administrative permit estimate, not audited spending, payroll, local purchasing, payment to PCL or proof of completion.

research_updates.title: Supplier audit preserves payment and locality gaps
research_updates.notes: Source families checked: PCL project records, SmartGov contractor rosters, operator vendor references, trade coverage, City procurement and agenda searches, and exact-address web/archive searches. Queries used 3500 Lyman, Flexential Chaska, ViaWest Chaska, PCL, contractor, supplier, vendor, subcontractor, procurement and payment. PCL is identified for the 2021 expansion and B24-1109; Metropolitan Mechanical/API HVAC for M24-0677 and value-less BP26-0072; Climate Makers/EVER for M26-0403 and overlapping P26-0523; and VINCO only on excluded cancelled permit B24-0504. No contract payment, subcontractor ledger, procurement total, vendor location, local-retention share, certified payroll or worker-residence record was located. This is a public supplier-payment gap, not evidence that no subcontracting, procurement or local spending occurred; contractor identity is not converted into supplier spending, indirect jobs, payroll or multiplier effects.

source.title: Flexential Data Center Expansion
source.notes: Contractor case study says PCL completed a tenant-driven expansion at the existing Chaska data center on June 30, 2021, involving an exterior mechanical yard, dry coolers, CRACs, generators, switchgear, raised floor, ceiling plenum and tenant office. It provides no contract value, paid amount, workforce, payroll, worker residence, local supplier share, power increment or water increment, so it supports chronology and supplier identity only.

research_updates.title: Operations audit adds scale but not employment
research_updates.notes: Source families checked: current and archived Flexential and ViaWest facility pages, opening and rebrand releases, careers and Workday postings, corporate reports, City employer tables, Minnesota DEED workforce/business-subsidy access points, OSHA establishment search and local-business coverage. Queries used Flexential Chaska, ViaWest Chaska, 3500 Lyman, Data Center Technician, employees, jobs, headcount, wages, payroll, residence, union, apprenticeship, careers, revenue and occupancy. Current operator materials support 160,838 square feet and 9 MW of critical-load UPS capacity. A Chaska vacancy and generic 24/7 staffing language do not disclose filled site FTE, wages, payroll, residence, occupancy, revenue or operating expenditure. OSHA's exact establishment query timed out, and indexed address searches produced only pre-project Entegris material; that unsuccessful bounded search cannot establish absence of inspections or injuries. No operating labor or output projection suitable for preservation was located.

source.title: Minneapolis - Chaska Data Center & Colocation
source.notes: Current operator facility page reports 9 MW of critical-load UPS capacity, a 1.4 PUE rating, 1,500 watts per square foot, N+1 cooling and 24/7 support. It does not publish annual metered electricity, peak demand, water, wastewater, emissions, occupancy, headcount, payroll, revenue or operating cost. Capacity is transcribed as an operating-scale stock, not usage or economic output.

research_updates.title: Fiscal audit verifies parcel payments and current owner
research_updates.notes: Source families checked: Carver County parcel, assessment, tax-statement and payment portals; City annual financial reports and budgets; taxpayer tables; and exact owner, parcel and address searches. Parcel 30.0590020 links FLEXENTIAL LLC to 3500 Lyman, 33.03 acres, industrial class 234, no listed TIF project and exact paid totals of $534,380 in 2023, $551,454 in 2024 and $582,406 in 2025. The 2026 $632,906 bill is entered separately; only one $316,453 installment was paid at review, so no full-year 2026 paid record is created. City Table 9 supports a separate Via West Inc. estimated-actual-value series for payable 2015-2022 ($11.6063 million to $13.894 million, peaking at $14.2431 million in 2021). Those unaudited company-city rows are not explicit parcel records and are not stitched to current Flexential values without a direct crosswalk. No recipient distribution, marginal service cost, incidence, causal increment or net fiscal result was located.

source.title: Carver County Property Information, parcel 30.0590020
source.notes: Interactive parcel query for 300590020 identifies FLEXENTIAL LLC, 3500 Lyman Boulevard, 33.03 deeded acres, industrial class 234, active non-homestead status, a blank TIF-project field and contribution to fiscal authority. Payment detail shows two $267,190 payments in 2023, two $275,727 payments in 2024 and two $291,203 payments in 2025. The 2026 account shows a $632,906 bill, including a $210 industrial solid-waste special assessment, and only the first $316,453 installment paid by the review date. The bill is preserved separately from paid totals. Annual totals span county, city, state, school and special-district components; they are not City-only receipts, taxpayer-incidence findings or net community benefit.

research_updates.title: Public-cost audit separates ViaWest certification from Stream rebates
research_updates.notes: Source families checked: Minnesota DEED certification lists and program summaries, Department of Revenue guidance, governing statute, the 2025 state tax-incentive evaluation, City tax-abatement notes, parcel TIF status, development-agreement archives and state/local financial reports. DEED separately lists certified ViaWest, Stream and Stream II projects; the Flexential parcel has no listed TIF project. Revenue guidance says the electricity exemption ended July 1, 2025. The state evaluation reports more than $90 million in statewide reduced revenue for 2015-2022 and modeled statewide employment/return findings, but no project allocation is defensible. Certification does not disclose ViaWest/Flexential refund or exemption value, qualifying purchases, compliance, clawback or disbursement. IP Stream rebates belong to the separate West Creek project. No Flexential-specific local payment, infrastructure subsidy, public-service cost or net public cost was located; that is non-quantification, not proof no benefit or cost existed.

source.title: Data Center Sales Tax Refund Projects
source.publisher: Minnesota Department of Employment and Economic Development
source.notes: Current state list separately identifies certified ViaWest Data Center - Chaska, Stream / IP Stream Minneapolis LLC and Stream II / IP Stream Minneapolis II LLC projects. Certification establishes program status but not refund value, qualifying-purchase amount, benefit recipient, claim date, clawback, compliance result or public expenditure. No facility-specific claim amount is published in the list.

research_updates.title: Resource audit finds capacity but no meter-level use
research_updates.notes: Source families checked: Chaska electric, water, sewer, budget, rate and billing sources; Minnesota PUC, MPCA What's in My Neighborhood and DNR indexes; Carver hazard planning; operator facility/ESG materials; and exact-address environmental searches. Operator pages report 9 MW critical-load UPS capacity and a 1.4 PUE rating, while the 2014 City budget aggregates ViaWest with several large users. MPCA site 145467 identifies active underground-tank activity TS0126051, 2015/2024 inspections, and a citation warning discovered September 5, 2024 and closed November 7, 2024 with no net penalty; zero documents or quantities are exposed. Exact PUC and DNR searches found no target-specific docket/permit, but these indexed non-results do not prove none exists. No facility meter, annual kWh, peak demand, bill, water, wastewater, generator runtime, fuel, actual emissions, utility-infrastructure cost or monetized effect was located. Fleet-wide figures are not allocated to Chaska.

source.title: City of Chaska 2014 Annual Budget Message
source.notes: The municipal electric budget anticipated commercial and industrial sales growth from multiple new large users, naming ViaWest, Stream, a medical-center addition, Beckman Coulter and residential growth together. City-wide Electric Fund revenue and sales cannot be allocated to ViaWest or converted into facility load, annual consumption, utility margin, infrastructure cost or local fiscal benefit.

research_updates.title: Community audit finds no quantified site transfer
research_updates.notes: Source families checked: Flexential/ViaWest ESG, news and community materials; City and county agendas/archives; Eastern Carver County Schools and Southwest Metro Intermediate District references; CareerForce and Minnesota DEED workforce sources; local nonprofit and recipient sites; and exact-address searches. Queries used Flexential Chaska, ViaWest Chaska, 3500 Lyman, grant, donation, sponsorship, nonprofit, school, training, workforce, apprenticeship, union and community benefit. No Chaska-specific recipient-reported cash or in-kind transfer, community-benefit agreement, workforce-program payment, school partnership, annual contribution, local-procurement pledge or facility-attributable value was located. The 2025 ESG material names nationwide organizations but does not locate spending at Chaska. This establishes a documentation gap, not that no community activity occurred; fleet-wide initiatives and qualitative engagement are not assigned to this parcel or monetized.

source.title: Flexential's 2025 ESG Report Details Progress in Sustainable Data Center Operations
source.notes: Company ESG release reports fleet-wide renewable-energy and closed-loop cooling measures. It does not disclose a Chaska-specific renewable share, electricity or water volume, wastewater, emissions, avoided cost, community contribution or monetized environmental effect, so fleet totals are not allocated to this facility.

economic_scope_note: Reviewed evidence batches at campus or company/county scope. No record is allocated to an individual inventory building. Source checking establishes what a document reports, not an independent audit or causal attribution. Monetary figures are nominal. Peak workforce is distinct from annual employment; source-year labels do not establish fiscal-year boundaries. Original forecasts remain forecasts until realization is verified. No cross-record benefit total is defined. Cumulative project costs are not annual expenditure. Tax receipts and incentive payments remain separate, with inferred taxpayer links disclosed. Contextual research updates do not count as economic amounts. Account tax bills are distinct from cash receipts and incentive-program fees. Tax years, calendar years and fiscal years retain their source basis; separate taxpayer accounts are not consolidated. Municipal developer rebates and taxpayer valuations have distinct subjects. Estimated actual property value and tax capacity are not tax receipts; payable-year valuations retain their earlier assessment date. Taxpayer values expressed in millions retain approximate precision and account-level separation. A current-year table can use an older valuation date and is not converted into an annual series. Facility real-property and business-personal-property accounts remain separate, and address-label discrepancies are disclosed. Michigan Industrial Facilities Tax accounts remain distinct from the underlying real parcel and from post-expiration personal-property accounts; annual account totals are not recipient-level government receipts. Permit construction values are administrative project amounts, not verified expenditure, and separate permits are not combined without proof that their scopes do not overlap. Repeated maintenance-year assessments are annual parcel stocks, not new investment flows. Mixed-use parcel assessments and taxable values are retained at whole-parcel scope and are not allocated to a data-center tenant or function by floor area. Operator-reported jobs supported remain distinct from direct employees and FTEs. Approved infrastructure grants are documented public commitments rather than verified disbursements or total public costs. Cumulative community funding remains separate from tax receipts, payroll and modeled multiplier effects. Reported facility power capacity is not measured electricity consumption or peak demand. Permit-listed emergency generators are not runtime, fuel-use or actual-emissions observations. A city largest-taxpayer table's personal-property assessment remains separate from the leasehold real-property account, tax bills, receipts and capital expenditure. TIF loan principal is financing rather than a grant or general-fund receipt; project-generated tax revenue pledged to repayment is retained as a separate public-financing flow and is not added to gross parcel distributions. Water-withdrawal and consumptive permit capacities are regulatory limits rather than measured use. Development-agreement local-labor preferences are requirements rather than realized participation, and operating employee snapshots remain distinct from customers' on-site staff and jobs forecasts. Audited City bond statements distinguish issuance draws, year-end principal, annual principal retired, interest and fees, pledged TIF revenue, debt-service-fund transfers and future principal-plus-interest commitments. These measures are not summed into a benefit or subsidy total. City pledged revenue, City debt-service-fund transfers and the private fund's project TIF revenue applied to loan repayment retain their separate source definitions because only the 2022 transfer and private-fund amount agree exactly. Developer testimony in public meeting minutes is retained as a source-attributed cumulative lower bound; local-contractor spending is not converted into payroll, worker counts, household spending or multiplier effects. Economic-improvement-district cost estimates and maximum owner assessments remain source projections until bond issuance, an assessment schedule, collections and expenditures are verified. A statutory financing cap is not a tax receipt, public expenditure or subsidy. Audited private equipment-financing balances are debt stocks rather than construction spending, public support or community benefit. Reported floor area and occupied-share values describe operating scale and utilization, not employment, revenue, power use or economic output. Contractor and engineer case studies document supplier roles and completion timing but do not establish payment amounts, worker residence, payroll or multiplier effects. State incentive contract amounts, expected jobs and paid-or-certified-to-date fields remain distinct; a zero paid/certified balance at an earlier reporting cutoff does not imply no later claims. Public charging-infrastructure awards are commitments rather than verified disbursements, private project investment or operating benefits. Qualitative payment descriptions without a defensible numeric bound remain research context rather than quantitative records. Program-reported actual qualified investment, certified tax-exemption value and certified tax-credit value remain separate cumulative measures; none is converted into annual spending, a cash grant, local revenue or causal impact. County Business Patterns observations are county-industry context, not project contributions: establishment counts are employer locations rather than data-center facilities, March employment is not an annual average, annual payroll spans the full NAICS cell, and disclosure noise, classification changes and geographic assignment limit comparisons. No CBP change is attributed to a study project. Project fragments: prj_study_im3_building_00052227492: Deep public-evidence audit for Flexential's Minneapolis-Chaska data center on parcel 30.0590020 at 3500 Lyman Boulevard. The review covered Carver County parcel, tax and property-record access points; City of Chaska permit, inspection, agenda, archive, budget, utility and annual-financial-report sources; Minnesota DEED, Revenue, statutory, environmental and utility-regulatory sources; federal workplace-safety search access; current and archived operator, predecessor, career and ESG materials; contractor and supplier references; and education, workforce and recipient-reported community sources for 2013-2026. Eighteen quantitative observations are preserved: a source-projected original investment lower bound; three later non-cumulative permit values; current floor area and critical-load UPS capacity; three annual parcel-tax payments; one current parcel-tax bill; and eight historical Via West Inc. estimated-actual-value observations. Stream's facilities at 1706 and 1708 West Creek Lane, the IP Stream Minneapolis LLC development agreement and its municipal rebates are outside the selected 3500 Lyman Boulevard project boundary and are not duplicated in this fragment; the six base Stream rebate rows require reassignment or removal from this target by the orchestrator because project fragments are append-only. Permit values are administrative estimates and are not summed because scopes may overlap. The current parcel-tax series includes all taxing jurisdictions and special assessments, not City-only receipts or net benefit, and the older citywide taxpayer series is not stitched to current parcel or Flexential values without a direct crosswalk. No synthesis fragment is added because direct observations and even a usable project projection were not found for construction labor, realized operating employment or payroll, supplier payments, metered energy or water, emissions, facility-specific incentive value, public-service costs, community transfers, or a causal county effect. prj_study_im3_building_00172739953: Corrective public-evidence and candidate-modeling audit for Switch Las Vegas NAP7, the individual real-property parcel and original SUPERNAP building at 7135 South Decatur Boulevard. The review covered Clark County assessor and ownership history, Treasurer, Accela permits, rights-of-way, planning, air quality, budgets and financial reports; Nevada incentive, tax and utility-regulatory sources; operator, SEC, workforce, supplier and contractor materials; and recipient-reported community records for 2005-2026. Six direct observations remain after the corrective pass; no wider Core Campus capital expenditure, combined incentive audit, later facility, personal property, tenant equipment, vendor equipment, company-wide employment or parcel-transfer price is recast as NAP7 contribution. One modeled synthesis is retained under the last-resort modeling gate: the fiscal-year 2027 real-property bill defines an exactly same-account assessed-liability public-service-cost break-even threshold. It is not actual public cost, collected revenue, jurisdictional receipt or a net fiscal result. Candidate models for investment, construction, suppliers, operations, resources, community benefits, net fiscal effects and county employment, GDP and wages were rejected for missing facility inputs, incompatible scope or timing, overlap, non-identification or lack of decision relevance. NAP7 employment, payroll, local supplier payments, metered electricity and water, personal-property tax, realized abatement, jurisdictional receipts, actual project-attributable public costs and net fiscal impact remain unobserved. prj_study_im3_building_00214321737: Second-pass public-evidence audit for Markley Group's Lowell data center at 2 Prince Avenue/1 Markley Way in Lowell, Middlesex County. The selected IM3 footprint is one building inside a three-building assessor parcel, so every added value remains at campus or company/county scope and is unallocated to the selected building. State and City records add Phase I forecasts, cumulative investment, operating-headcount, TIF-savings and incentive evidence; the assessor and tax portal add annual real-property stocks and one complete billed-tax year; permit reports add discrete administrative construction values and contractor names; MassDEP adds a permit-listed generator count; and a recipient page verifies one community contribution. Forecasts, cumulative values, parcel stocks, billed taxes, permit values, permit-authorized equipment, white-space area and recipient funding remain distinct and non-additive. Searches of planning and permit files, incentive and compliance reports, assessor and fiscal records, utility and environmental materials, operator disclosures, contractor and supplier pages, workforce and procurement records, community recipients, archives and repository county panels found no audited annual construction outlay, construction workforce or payroll, vendor payments or local-purchase share, facility payroll, metered annual electricity, project-attributable utility upgrade cost, annual water series matching the evidence vocabulary, wastewater, actual emissions, cash tax receipts, marginal public-service cost, fiscal net or causal county outcome. No model is added because the missing allocation and expenditure anchors cannot be bounded defensibly and Markley is not a clean first data-center entry in Middlesex County. prj_study_im3_building_00364289074: Corrective public-source audit for Microsoft's data-center property at 5150 Rogers Road and explicitly labeled wider Microsoft/Bexar County activity. Exact-site ordinance, permit, appraisal, and tax-account records remain separate from later campuses and regional disclosures; the three appraisal accounts and two taxable-account payments are not consolidated. Permit value is administrative, the original investment and employment figures are commitments, the 2013 employment threshold is a reported lower bound, and the water quantity is a projection rather than metered consumption. No Bexar-and-Medina total is allocated to this property. Annual construction expenditure, construction labor and residence, supplier payments, operating payroll and purchases, recipient-level tax distributions, marginal public-service cost, electricity consumption, water withdrawal or consumption, wastewater, actual emissions, and a recurring facility-level community series remain unobserved after the documented searches. prj_study_im3_building_00377585075: Corrective DET01 evidence audit. Official parcel, permit, tax, water-account, state-certificate, EPA and operator records are retained as direct observations or clearly labeled source forecasts. Conflicting floor-area figures remain separate because their reporting definitions differ. Construction cost, realized jobs, supplier payments, community funding, electricity, emissions, wastewater, actual public-service cost and causal county effects remain unbounded rather than being filled with transferred assumptions. prj_study_im3_building_00460089167: Corrective primary-source audit adds current Andale parcel assessment, contractor-reported campus floor area, and two recipient- or government-reported Meta community grants. The search trail records useful and negative results across identity, tax, construction, jobs, suppliers, utilities, water, permits, public costs, incentives, community funding, and county comparison inputs. Campus-wide facts remain unallocated to the selected inventory building, overlapping community amounts are not added together, and unavailable supplier, payroll, utility-billing, discharge, generator, and marginal-service-cost amounts remain explicit gaps. prj_study_im3_building_00464097467: Second-pass public-evidence audit for Apple's Washoe County data-center campus at 21505 Reno Technology Parkway West and its 2024 expansion application. GOED audit findings, application forecasts, county permit values, parcel assessments, a water-right allocation, operator-reported electricity use, and recipient-reported donation bands remain separate evidence states and scopes. Permit values are administrative amounts and are not summed because overlapping scopes cannot be ruled out. Assessment values are parcel stocks, not investment or tax receipts. The 125 acre-foot water right is regulatory capacity, not measured use. Food Bank gifts are company-region transfers, not campus-attributable annual spending. No campus total is allocated to the selected mapped building; the four-building campus, later buildout cases, downtown Reno warehouse, supporting renewable projects, fire-station parcel, and more-than-200-person support statement are not collapsed into one footprint. No Switch Citadel or Storey County amount enters this fragment. Vendor payments, worker residence, taxes received by jurisdiction, realized 2024 abatement, same-scope public-service cost, wastewater, and building-level electricity or water remain unobserved. prj_study_im3_building_00598261190: Corrective public-evidence and last-resort modeling audit for the State Farm data center at 24400 West Valley Parkway in Olathe, Kansas. The account adds the exact-address Kansas HPIP FY2020 capital-investment entry to the City permit and SEC property evidence while keeping the HPIP amount, permit values, SEC estimated cumulative capital spending, parcel assessments, tax bills and tax payments distinct and non-additive. The search trail covers parcel and fiscal records, construction and suppliers, operations and workforce, incentives, utility and environmental regulation, community activity, planning, public costs and county outcomes. No site-level employment, payroll, supplier payment, community transfer, metered electricity or water, claimed incentive amount, actual marginal public-service cost, net fiscal position or attributable county effect is inferred from public material. prj_study_im3_building_00626785488: Second-pass public-evidence audit for the individual 654,433-square-foot IM3-mapped building footprint within Meta's Los Lunas data-center campus at 4250 Messenger Loop NW. The review covered the original campus chronology and 2016 industrial-revenue-bond package; Village budgets, audits, LEDA and dedicated infrastructure funds, planning, building, traffic, fire and water records; Valencia County assessor and clerk access; New Mexico economic-development, workforce, Construction Industries Division, Public Regulation Commission and Environment Department materials; PNM regulatory filings; Meta operator, SEC, contractor, career and grant materials; recipient-reported community records; and federal environmental and county-outcome access through September 6, 2026. Fifteen new direct observations are added alongside the two retained baseline observations, all at unallocated campus, company-county or supporting-infrastructure scope because no public source crosswalks the selected IM3 footprint to a separately named building, permit, parcel, workforce, utility meter or fiscal account. The later 2021 two-building expansion, 2023 three-building expansion load, 2025 AI expansion, off-site renewable projects, tenant equipment and other Meta facilities are excluded. No synthesis fragment is added because the selected building's operating date is not identified and the original six-building construction and operating sequence cannot support an isolated county treatment. Building-level capital expenditure, permits and fees, payroll, resident employment, supplier payments, metered electricity and water, utility bills, tax or PILOT payments, cash value of realized abatements, public-service costs and net fiscal results remain unobserved. prj_study_im3_building_00664938835: Second-pass public-evidence audit for Expedient's adaptive reuse of the pre-existing data-center building at 4777 W Ironwood Drive. The review searched Franklin planning, agenda, assessment, permit, water and sewer materials; Milwaukee County tax and deed-record access points; Wisconsin DOR, WEDC, DFI and PSC records; operator press, specification, career, ESG and community pages; lease, financing, carrier and vendor disclosures; and archived official pages for 2007-2026. Opening-day and current operator specifications remain separate dated snapshots because the reported area and capacity changed. The county portal now establishes a 2021-2025 parcel-tax principal series, but not Expedient's incidence under the lease. The 2022 ownership transfer, assessments, estimated permit values, tax payments and hiring plan remain non-additive. No source was found for actual construction outlays, realized site employment or payroll, local procurement, Milwaukee-area community transfers, metered resources, project-attributable public costs or a fiscal net. prj_study_im3_building_00844389014: Second-pass direct-evidence audit for Google Clarksville in Montgomery County, Tennessee. The review covered Tennessee Comptroller industrial-development-board PILOT filings for 2019-2025; the Montgomery County assessor GIS parcel service and Trustee tax-bill portal; parcel-linked stormwater files; Clarksville-Montgomery County Regional Planning Commission materials; IDB, county-commission and city agenda archives; state and federal environmental portals; operator location, environmental, economic-impact and watershed materials; utility annual reports; and public workforce, contractor, procurement and recipient sources. Fifty-eight incremental quantitative observations are preserved: thirteen annual Foxman LLC estimated-actual-property-value stocks, eighteen account-level appraised-value stocks, eighteen account-level zero tax levies, a realized opening-period employee snapshot, a construction-workforce projection, and seven recipient-specific community contributions. The direct Trustee records resolve the ordinary tax bills as 0%-taxable, zero-assessed-taxable-value, zero-levy bills; they do not resolve the separate contractual PILOT payments left blank in state filings, and the portal's generic paid/zero-balance label is not treated as a cash receipt. The selected inventory key is one building, while parcel, account and environmental evidence is campus or company/county scoped and remains unallocated. Statewide investment and modeled impact totals, shared Alabama-Tennessee renewable capacity, regional watershed contributions, vendor presence without paid-contract evidence, and proposals for later Building 13 work are excluded from canonical project records. A single optional synthesis reproduces the operator's 2024 Montgomery County water-consumption identity at unallocated location scope; no multiplier, supplier-retention, fiscal-net, public-cost, energy, payroll or causal county model is created. prj_study_im3_building_00888253616: Second-pass public-evidence audit for NTT Silicon Valley SV1 at 1160 Walsh Avenue, Santa Clara. The review reconciles the planning-era 1150 Walsh address to APN 224-58-003; adds the finaled principal permit, its administrative job value, current operator specifications, emergency-generator authorization and the parcel's regular-bill payment history; and leaves supplemental bills separate to avoid double counting. Public sources still do not establish realized site employment or payroll, total project investment, supplier payments, project-specific community transfers, metered resources, or project-attributable public-service costs. prj_study_im3_building_01024051963: Corrective source audit for the Meta Eagle Mountain campus and the selected IM3 building footprint in Utah County. Campus, company-county, and supporting-infrastructure observations remain explicitly unallocated to the selected building; later expansion areas and unrelated Eagle Mountain data-center developers are excluded unless a source establishes continuity. prj_study_im3_building_01073720208: Second-pass public-evidence audit for Google's Council Bluffs data-center activity, retaining the selected inventory building as the project key while leaving campus, taxpayer-account, company-county, and state-award facts at their reported scopes. The audit distinguishes completed IEDA contracts 08-HQJC-030 and 12-HQJP-051 from the 2022 award still in performance; permit valuations remain administrative amounts rather than expenditure; assessed and taxable values remain stocks; bills remain distinct from payments; and community grants remain recipient- and period-specific. The Pottawattamie County tax portal now supplies a paid 2018-2024 series for the principal Tetra parcel and an unpaid 2025 bill for the newer Questa parcel. No value is inferred for sales-tax exemptions, the local abatement schedule, franchise-fee adjustment, electricity, supplier retention, building-level water, marginal public-service cost, or net fiscal position. Models without defensible project allocation or transferable parameters were removed even though that leaves the eight-category account incomplete. prj_study_im3_building_01132541700: Corrective primary-source audit adds two county taxable-account observations, state-verified incentive-compliance thresholds, current operator-reported jobs and community funding, one county-received grant, facility electricity use, supporting renewable capacity, and the 2018 expansion forecast. The search trail covers identity, land use, permits, assessor and fiscal records, incentives, public costs, utilities, water, suppliers, courts, bonds, community funding, and federal county outcomes. Most public evidence covers the multi-building Henrico campus or Scout Development's county account and remains unallocated to the selected inventory building; overlapping funding and investment figures are not summed, and unavailable supplier payments, utility bills, tax receipts, incentive costs, payroll, and marginal public-service costs remain explicit gaps. prj_study_im3_campus_00019988712: Second-pass direct-evidence audit for Meta's Prineville data-center campus at 735 SW Connect Way in Prineville, Crook County. The selected IM3 entity is the campus, not one PRN building, every Vitesse-owned county parcel, Apple's separate campus, or Meta's statewide and global portfolios. The fragment now separates annual company-level potential additional tax from facility-level 2024-25 exemption values, taxable Vitesse totals from exempt account values, billed tax from payment status, agreement schedules from realized distributions, and one exact permit valuation from construction expenditure. Business Oregon identifies all three long-term-rural-zone facilities; Crook County's public assessor portal resolves 25 current Vitesse/Meta accounts across nine map-tax-lot strings and provides an annual history for exact-address account 19380; and Oregon ePermitting supplies an exact permit, contractor, project description and job value. Projections remain projections, overlapping summary/detail tax records are not summed, and multi-company budgets are not allocated. Realized Meta-only PILOT distributions, a reconciled all-account exemption roll, construction payroll/job-years, supplier payments/local-spend share, same-scope public-service costs, campus water bills, and causal county effects remain unavailable. prj_study_im3_campus_00231769626: Second-pass public-evidence audit for Google's The Dalles campus in Wasco County. The fragment preserves the baseline 2023-2025 Google LLC and Design LLC tax-bill and assessed-value series and the documented $28.5 million water-infrastructure project, and adds only incremental evidence. Business Oregon supplies a dated three-facility operating snapshot and separately bounded Project 1 and Project 2 SIP forecasts; City of The Dalles planning files and contractor/permit records document later River Road construction without treating permit valuations as spending. A recipient record verifies one local grant. Searches of assessor and treasurer records, budgets and agreements, planning and permit systems, utility and environmental records, operator ESG/careers materials, contractors, suppliers, workforce sources, nonprofit recipients, archives and structured portals found no audited construction outlay, local supplier spend, facility payroll, employee residence, project-attributable utility cost or load, realized abatement ledger, same-scope public service cost, or fiscal net. Statewide Google totals and system-wide utility loads are excluded from campus claims. prj_study_im3_campus_00675108684: Project-scoped audit of Microsoft’s bounded Boydton/East Coast/LVL campus in Mecklenburg County adds direct parcel, permit, expansion, performance, portfolio, infrastructure, construction and community evidence. Reported actuals remain distinct from announcement projections, and countywide portfolio figures remain unallocated. A dedicated last-resort eligibility pass adds only deterministic normalization and same-period arithmetic: the five-year average of reported portfolio property taxes, its explicitly conditional public-cost break-even identity, and annual sums of identified FY2024 and FY2025 LVL/Herbert Fund 301 components; achieved phase investment and jobs plus resource/construction measures remain unsummed because their overlap, timing, or required inputs are unresolved.
modeled_scope_note: Modeled contribution accounts for Apple Mesa / Maricopa County, Switch Citadel / Storey County, and Digital Crossroad Hammond / Lake County. Every required account category and county-comparison module contains sourced evidence or a visibly labeled modeled value. Public support is not netted against unmatched local revenues, unavailable public-service cost is represented by a break-even threshold rather than an invented net margin, county comparisons are descriptive rather than causal, and low-confidence transferred benchmarks remain explicit. Project fragments: prj_study_im3_building_00172739953: Last-resort NAP7 modeling pass under study-modeling-policy-1.3.0. The only retained synthesis is an exact, same-property-account fiscal-year 2027 assessed-liability public-service-cost break-even identity. It uses the directly observed property-tax bill without estimating actual public cost, cash collections, recipient distributions or net fiscal impact. Investment, construction, supplier, operations, resource, community and county outcome candidates were rejected because compatible NAP7 inputs or credible identification are unavailable. prj_study_im3_building_00364289074: Corrective residual modeled account for Microsoft San Antonio. Eight transferred construction, labor, procurement, operating, and household-output scenarios were removed because their arbitrary capital shares, forecast-realization cases, local-purchase assumptions, and Virginia coefficients were not bounded by project observations. Only three low-confidence descriptive county comparisons remain: each uses the project's documented operating-by 2013 anchor and official Bexar County outcome data, has a finite fit-sensitivity envelope, and explicitly makes no causal attribution. The account intentionally remains incomplete because no defensible direct observation or residual model closes the supplier category. prj_study_im3_building_00377585075: Corrective DET01 synthesis. Only exact same-period tax-account arithmetic, its explicitly conditional public-cost break-even identity and a unit conversion of displayed municipal meter history remain. Construction, employment, supplier, household, electricity, cooling, emissions, wastewater and county-effect models were removed because the audit did not bound the missing project inputs. This account is intentionally incomplete where direct evidence remains unbounded. prj_study_im3_building_00460089167: Corrective audit retains six bounded residual calculations only: FY2025 county tax retained after the provisionally linked incentive, the identical marginal-service-cost break-even threshold, conversion of Meta-reported 2024 water withdrawal with source rounding, and three noncausal county comparison gaps with fit sensitivity. Ten models based on arbitrary capital timing, cost shares, FTE ratios, transferred operating/construction multipliers, fleet PUE, or wastewater ratios are removed. Supplier/local-procurement evidence remains unavailable, so the project is intentionally incomplete rather than backfilled. prj_study_im3_building_00464097467: Second-pass modeled contribution account after an expanded public-evidence audit. Direct county permits now cover historical construction values, assessor rolls cover a main-campus parcel stock, a county action covers water-right capacity, Apple reports 2025 campus electricity use, and recipient reports bound two community gifts. Those observations supersede the need for a modeled community proxy but do not supply Apple contractor job-years, construction payroll, annual operating payroll, supplier payments, taxes received, or public-service cost. The construction base therefore retains only the packet's explicit $163 million construction forecast and excludes equipment and historical capital; wide 0.5-1.5 transfer sensitivities expose the mismatch in the last-resort direct construction coefficients. The unsupported local-purchase-share and Virginia induced-output models are removed. No net-fiscal value or public-service-cost break-even is published. County outcome gaps remain descriptive benchmark applications with fit-sensitivity intervals and no causal-design metadata. prj_study_im3_building_00598261190: Dedicated last-resort model-eligibility pass for State Farm Olathe under study-modeling-policy-1.3.0. Four bounded syntheses are retained: the exact 2025 parcel-tax-payment identity as a same-account public-service-cost break-even threshold, plus low-confidence descriptive 2024 Johnson County GDP, employment and wage comparison gaps using the repository's pre-2016 inverse-distance benchmark. No estimate is an observed cost, net fiscal result or causal facility effect. Supplier/local-spend and community-allocation candidates, an HPIP credit counterfactual, and causal county designs are rejected because the project-specific inputs, scope matches, non-overlap proof or identification conditions recorded in the evidence fragment are absent. prj_study_im3_building_00664938835: Second-pass Expedient Milwaukee / Franklin syntheses retained only after a documented 2007-2026 public-source audit. The account keeps a clearly labeled 2022 ownership-transfer anchor, a PB25-0303-only construction allocation sensitivity, an exact tax-equal public-cost break-even threshold, a capacity-based electricity engineering sensitivity, and three descriptive county comparison gaps. It removes transferred construction job-years, assumed local-purchase shares, supplier and household output extrapolations, and a duplicate modeled tax row because public sources did not establish realized site employment, supplier geography, household capture, or a need to restate the direct tax observations. PM25-0174 remains excluded for possible overlap. No synthesis is an observed result or fiscal net. prj_study_im3_building_00844389014: Second-pass model review retains one bounded resource identity only. It reproduces Google-reported 2024 Montgomery County water consumption as withdrawal minus discharge after converting displayed million-gallon values to gallons, with a rounding envelope. Direct searches of Clarksville utility/public-works pages, county stormwater records, TDEC/EPA portals and CDE/TVA materials did not surface a building meter, utility bill or a compatible canonical observed-water metric. The amount remains unallocated across the location and inventory buildings; discharge may be engineering-estimated. No transferred multiplier, supplier-retention assumption, energy proxy, fiscal result, public-cost threshold, payroll estimate or causal county outcome is modeled. prj_study_im3_building_00888253616: Residual synthesis after the SV1 public-source audit. It retains one exact tax-equal public-cost break-even threshold and three reproducible but low-confidence county comparison gaps. The county gaps use 2013-2020 pre-opening histories and an inverse-distance-weighted 20-county benchmark; very wide fit envelopes are retained because Santa Clara County matches poorly. No model converts capacity to consumption, permit value to jobs, or unidentified vendor and community activity to local benefits. prj_study_im3_building_01073720208: Second-pass governed synthesis for Google Council Bluffs. Construction job-years use only two directly observed September 2025 city permit valuations and transfer the published Prince William County prototype coefficients as benchmark equivalents; the four channels are separated and protected by one aggregation. No Pottawattamie County supplier-retention share is imposed because the public audit found contractor names but no payment or vendor-residence ledger. The water row is the unallocated Google Council Bluffs location identity reported for 2024, not a building allocation. No local abatement, exemption realization, franchise-fee amount, electric load, public-service cost, break-even threshold, or net fiscal result is modeled. County outcome gaps remain descriptive benchmark applications with fit-sensitivity ranges and no causal attribution. prj_study_im3_building_01132541700: Four bounded syntheses are retained after direct-record search: one deterministic conversion of Meta's rounded 2024 Henrico water-withdrawal observation and three governed, descriptive county comparison gaps. No construction, operating, supplier, household, tax-receipt, incentive-cost, or public-service-cost model is added because the public record lacks the needed project-specific bases and arbitrary allocation shares would create false precision. Every retained estimate is visibly modeled, unallocated to the selected building, non-additive, and noncausal. prj_study_im3_campus_00019988712: Residual synthesis after the Meta Prineville direct-evidence audit. One medium-confidence unit conversion carries Meta's rounded 2024 facility-level water-withdrawal observation from megaliters to gallons because the shared direct register has no compatible annual-withdrawal metric. The three low-confidence county benchmark comparisons were removed: even with fit-sensitivity envelopes and explicit non-causal labels, they do not materially improve decisions about this campus and remain vulnerable to concurrent Meta expansions, Apple's separate campus and unrelated county changes. No supplier, construction, payroll, household-spending, tax-abatement, public-service-cost or fiscal-net model is retained because local inputs and same-scope evidence are insufficient. prj_study_im3_campus_00231769626: Residual synthesis after the Google The Dalles public-source audit. project_description: Flexential's Minneapolis-Chaska facility is a single adaptive-reuse colocation data center operated by Flexential on parcel 30.0590020 at 3500 Lyman Boulevard in Chaska, Carver County, Minnesota. ViaWest acquired the former Entegris headquarters in 2013, renovated it, and opened more than 70,000 square feet of raised floor in April 2014; Peak 10 combined with ViaWest in 2017 and the business adopted the Flexential name in 2018. The current operator reports a 160,838-square-foot footprint and 9 MW of critical-load UPS capacity; later tenant-driven expansion and Phase 5 work at this parcel are separate from the original conversion, and Stream's 1708 West Creek Lane facility is outside this project boundary.
